# LARGE UNIFORM BACILLI IN AN ANAEROBIC BOTTLE

Large uniform bacilli in an anaerobic bottle usually suggest clostridium, a potentially severe pathogen. Combination therapy is recommended for necrotizing infections as clindamycin has the theoretical benefit of inhibiting toxin production.

References

- Medical Letter Choice of Antimicrobials 2010, 8.94
- Sanford keyword: Clostridium perfingens
- Stevens et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases 2014 59.2
Therapy:
## Empirical treatment of mild to moderate infection

Penicillin G 4 million units IV q4h (Cost $$)R

For patients with non-severe penicillin allergy
Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q24h (Cost $) M

For patients with severe penicillin allergy
Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h (Cost $) R

## Empirical treatment of severe or necrotizing infection

Penicillin G 4 million units IV q4h (Cost $$) R <AND> clindamycin 900 mg
IV q8h (Cost $$) [H,O]
Inpt: ORZID2 GMENU INT LRG RODS ANAEROBIC BOT
